G03.why: Same asked quantity (constant giving infinitely many solutions of a one-variable linear equation); G03's constant sits in both coefficient and right side with a c = -4 trap, so the reasoning extends beyond matching coefficients.
Parameter-in-coefficient linear equation solution count (no-solution version); same 'coefficient vanishes' idea, different case.

G04.why: Change in output of a linear model for a given change in input (slope x change); G04 adds a minutes-to-hours conversion.

G06.why: Line through parametric points (k, 3k); reversed direction (find k from slope vs. find slope with constant canceling).

G07.why: System with no solution for a parameter; G07 puts the parameter in two coefficients (a^2 = 12) and needs a distinct-lines check.
Parameter conditions on a 2x2 linear system (infinitely-many version).

G08.why: Linear equation with fractional binomial terms ((x-4)/3 = (x+2)/5); G08 uses subtraction with a distribution-of-minus trap.

G10.why: Line through the same point (2, 5) plus one extra condition; asks x-intercept from m + b = 8 rather than slope from equal intercepts. Consider changing the point.

G12.why: Same 'solutions lost by dividing by a variable factor' trap (x^3 = x); different equation form and asked quantity (sum).

G13.why: Radical equation with an extraneous root; G13 uses u = sqrt(x) substitution rather than squaring a linear right side.
Radical equation solved for x (two square roots); same skill, different structure.

G16.why: Factoring a trinomial with leading coefficient > 1; G16 asks a + b + c + d of the factored form instead of picking a factor.

G17.why: Evaluate a related exponential from a given one (2^(3x) = 64 -> 2^x); G17 rewrites 27^x * 3^-x as 9^x.

G18.why: Reverse of the same identity family: ACT gives x + 1/x = 5 and asks x^2 + 1/x^2; G18's answer is exactly 5 = x + 1/x, so the two would cue each other in one set.
Sum of a number and its reciprocal (solve for x); reversed direction.

G20.why: Equal outputs at two inputs imply symmetry about the axis (f(1) = f(9)); G20 asks the unknown input a instead of a value.

G21.why: Rational equation with denominator x - 1 / x - 2 and an extraneous solution; G21 asks which constant makes the only candidate extraneous.

G22.why: Sign of a polynomial with a squared factor (x + 2)^2(x - 3); G22 counts integers with p > 0 and has a negative leading factor (3 - x).
Double root touches without changing sign; same key fact, different ask.

G24.why: Median from a frequency table over values 0-4; G24 inverts it (least unknown frequency making median 3).
Values of an unknown that keep a median fixed; list not frequency table.

G25.why: Interpreting a margin of error for a 52% poll ('which conclusion is best supported'); G25 compares two polls' intervals (overlap). Same opening number 52%; consider changing it.

G26.why: Combining two percent changes multiplicatively on a subgroup share; SAT asks the new share, G26 asks percent change in the subgroup count.

G28.why: Right-triangle trig from a given tangent (tan = 2 -> cos); G28 derives tan = 3 from sin = 3 cos and asks the hypotenuse from a leg.

G29.why: Same algebra core: x^2 + y^2 = 29, xy = 10 -> (x + y)^2. G29 is a^2 + b^2 = 100, ab = 40 -> (a + b)^2 in a right-triangle context; strongest match in the set.
Right triangle linking legs, hypotenuse and area (legs x, x + 7, hyp 13 -> area); reversed direction.
Perimeter of a right triangle from the hypotenuse plus one more fact.

within_list_cues.why: Both hinge on converting a per-minute rate in a linear model to per-hour (x60); used together the first teaches the trap of the second.

Both ask 'for what constant does the equation degenerate', solved by finding the value that zeroes a factor (c - 4 / x - 1); one cues the method for the other. G07 belongs to the same parameter-condition cluster.
Same 'do not divide by an expression that may be zero' lesson (c - 4 vs x - 3); G03's explanation gives away G12's trap.
G27's 6-8 legs imply hypotenuse 10; next to G29 (hypotenuse 10) it primes the false 6-8-10 assumption (area 24, not 20). Mis-cue rather than answer leak.

official_sat_notes: No idea is a near-copy of a released official SAT item that I can identify with confidence. G07 (parameter in two coefficients, no-solution system), G25 (two-poll margin-of-error overlap) and G04 (interpreting a per-minute coefficient per hour) follow common released Bluebook item styles but with their own numbers; G18, G27 and G30 are classic contest exercises rather than SAT items.
